en: It was like a plot of land that the law had marked out and that stayed empty. The IOC is the building put up on that plot. It is the legal category for the case in which what you consume depends, structurally, on an environment that the platform runs, adjusts and can change.

The IOC does not call for a separate system, with rules of its own for the digital world. It is an update of a reading that already fits within the Brazilian Consumer Protection Code (Código de Defesa do Consumidor, CDC) and the constitutional principles that underpin it. In other words, the law already had the tools, and what was missing was pointing them at the right place.

A bundle is a set of threads tied together, and enjoyment is the use and benefit you get out of something. The name describes the set of uses, signs and positions that a product of this kind offers, all of them run by the platform for as long as the relationship lasts. The bundle goes hand in hand with the IOC, which is the legal name for what you bought, and that product is itself an enjoyment bundle sustained over time. That is why, of the four questions that show whether a case is of this kind, the first is which bundle was promised.

Your skin is a product, but a product of a special kind. You do not take it home, and its use, what it shows to others and the place it gives you exist only while the platform keeps the environment running. The legal category for this product is the Immaterial Object of Consumption, or IOC.

The path brings in nine concepts of its own and others drawn from other fields of knowledge, each one accounting for one part of the problem. Read in isolation, they would be labels. Together, they speak the same language, and the center of that language is the IOC, because without it the others lose their footing.

The IOC is the building on that plot. And an empty plot has a cost. While a loss lacks a category and a criterion, it is hard to show and hard to claim, and every gap that lasts tends to become someone's business model.
When is there an IOC?

There is an Immaterial Object of Consumption (IOC) whenever the utility consumed presents itself as a position of enjoyment sustained by continuous private governance. In that case there is an immaterial product in a legally relevant sense, and art. 3, § 1, of the CDC applies1. The category gives concrete form to the notion of immaterial product that the law already provided for and reads it as a governed enjoyment bundle.

Open auditability is the minimum threshold of external verifiability that makes it possible to reconstruct what the supplier changed, when, why and with what effect, whenever the change or the sanction relevantly affects the enjoyment of an IOC. The requirement arises within the CDC, has a defined scope and does not yield to secrecy or to technical complexity.

The protected legal interests are what the injury reaches when the platform downgrades, sanctions or erases the position of enjoyment of an IOC, even when formal access remains open, and they are called personal integrity, symbolic identity and biographical continuity. They are defined by public criteria and are tied to civil personality, which is why the loss of a history or a title can go beyond the loss of an item.

The hypothesis is that this update depends on a legal-analytical category capable of capturing the specificity of digital goods in a platform environment. That category is the Immaterial Object of Consumption (IOC), an infrastructure-concept that gives concrete form to the immaterial product of art. 3, § 1, of the CDC1 and shifts the focus from the conformity of the corporeal object to the governance of the functional and symbolic architectures of the experience. The factual vulnerability of art. 4, I, of the CDC2 takes on a form of its own there, tied to mediation by signs and interfaces and intensified by hypercuratorial anticipation, which projects images of performance, reward and future experience without offering, in the same measure, real conditions of verification. Abusive teleology makes it possible to qualify, under strict criteria, the situations in which the architecture is designed to exploit that vulnerability systematically, and protection must also cover the functional integrity of the goods and the personal and symbolic identity of the user.

The answer does not lie in a new law or in a microsystem for games or platforms. The IOC is an interpretive update already internal to the CDC and derived from the constitutional principles that inform it, and the reconstruction works on existing law, without normative invention. Behind it lies a reading of Consumer Law as a deliberately expandable technical idiom, made to recognize shifting asymmetries and to capture abuses that do not announce themselves as deviations.

Functional value equivalence is the criterion that judges whether the alteration of an IOC preserved, in substantial terms, what justified the acquisition. The test rests on art. 51, XIII, of the CDC1, reaches the appearance of an item when that appearance is what was bought, and leads to recomposition.

This path reconstructs, for lawyers, judges, members of the Public Prosecutor's Office and students, the legal regime of the IOC. Each chapter starts from a problem, shows why the ordinary reading falls short and arrives at what can be demonstrated and claimed.

The Immaterial Object of Consumption (IOC) is the category that qualifies as an immaterial product, under Article 3, paragraph 1, of the Brazilian Consumer Protection Code (CDC)<1><2>1</2></1>, the utility that only exists as a position of enjoyment sustained by private governance. Without this qualification the case seems to have no object, and with it the jurist knows what to demonstrate in court.

Functional value equivalence is the criterion that judges whether the alteration of an IOC preserved, in substantial terms, what justified the acquisition. The test rests on Article 51, item XIII, of the CDC<1><2>3</2></1>, reaches the appearance of an item when that appearance is what was bought, and leads to restoration.

Intellectual property enters the regime of the IOC as part of the infrastructure through which the platform defines what can be accessed, kept, altered, withdrawn, audited and contested, and not as a topic parallel or superior to consumer protection. Exclusivity has come to organize competition and enjoyment, and the social function, read from Article 5, item XXIX, of the Federal Constitution<1><2>4</2></1>, makes it a field of reconciliation with the CDC.

Remedies close the examination of a conflict over an IOC, because they answer what to do with the injury once the object has been qualified, the change reconstructed, equivalence assessed and the evidence organized. Primacy belongs to functional restoration and regime correction, and compensation comes after them, not in their place.
The regime of the IOC for jurists, from the problem to evidence and remedies, in fifteen chapters.

The traditional examination asks, separately, whether the clause existed, whether the information was technically available and whether the advertisement contained literal falsehood. On platforms, information, advertising and abusive practices operate together in forming expectation, urgency, trust and tolerance for frustration, so that the object of control becomes the integrated decision-making arrangement through which the platform organizes the consumer's adhesion and permanence, distributing visibility, scarcity, comparability and promise of value. The sensitivity is greater in the IOC, because the decision falls on governed future experience, continuously modulated by architecture, curation and private sanction, and the initial expectation comes to form part of the very legal substance of the enjoyment.

When the enjoyment of an IOC depends on signs, visibility and equivalences that exist only while the environment maintains them, the acquisition comes to depend on an ecosystem that provides intelligibility, comparison and the possibility of sanction and that defines, in practice, access, permanence and hierarchies. The core of the problem is institutional. The platform does not merely mediate a bilateral relationship between supplier and acquirer, because it organizes at the same time the normative content of the environment and the means of enforcing it.

The point finds support in Zelmo Denari, Antonio Herman Benjamin, Nelson Nery Jr. and Miragem, and its application is not exhausted by the text of the Code either. Art. 7 of the CDC9 opens the microsystem to other sources, and Marques reads that opening as an updating interface, which integrates the rights secured by external legislation, but not the limits on those rights, so that it reinforces protection and never serves as a privatist escape route. Art. 47 of the CDC10, which requires clauses to be interpreted in the way most favorable to the consumer, already signals that unilaterally drafted ambiguities do not turn imposed precariousness into legal normality, and art. 4, I, III and VI, of the CDC11 and art. 6, I, III, IV, VI and VIII, of the CDC12 show a protection that applies to risk, opacity, deception, evidentiary asymmetry and unfair methods. On platforms, information, verifiability, permanence and contestation cannot be technical favors administered by whoever designs the environment. The regime of the IOC is not an extravagant construction, because utility that depends on continuous governance, unilateral reconfiguration, technical opacity and asymmetric distribution of evidence is a constitutionally qualified case for containing asymmetries.

Carried over to digital consumption, the diagnosis makes it possible to read electronic games, streaming platforms and social networks as manifestations of a technique that works as an environment, in which interfaces, algorithms, reward systems and mechanisms of artificial scarcity are organized by criteria of efficiency, retention and continuous governance. It is from this operation that the category of the Immaterial Object of Consumption (IOC) emerges, an object of functional and continuing existence, inseparable from the technical infrastructure that gives it access, utility, stability and practical meaning. Hence the inadequacy of a strictly material reading of consumption, because the central problem is no longer only the existence of a defect in an isolated product and comes to include the way technique organizes the possibilities of use, permanence, loss or degradation over time.
Why is the environment the condition of possibility of the IOC?

It is on this ground that the rest of the regime is built. The question is no longer only the content of the promise and comes to include the way it becomes operative and the mediations that shape enjoyment without letting themselves be fully verified by the recipient. The purpose inscribed in design can be reconstructed as a structure of purpose, and requirements such as open auditability and functional value equivalence will come to operate as minimum parameters of legitimacy for exchanges mediated by systems. The techno-media environment, therefore, is not an external setting of the IOC, but its condition of possibility.
